title: HubSpot routing requirements for PLG→Sales signals (fields, ownership, suppression, workflows)
creator: Chris Osei
description:
Context
We are implementing a PLG-led→sales-assisted expansion motion by emitting high-signal usage/intent triggers and routing them into HubSpot with consistent ownership rules, deduplication, suppression, and a follow-up cadence (tasks + sequences). This ticket defines the HubSpot-side contract: required fields/objects, workflow behavior, and SLAs so Engineering can write events and Biz Systems can configure workflows safely.

Out of scope
- Final trigger thresholds/scoring logic (PM-412 + design spec).
- Copywriting for sequences/talk tracks (sales enablement playbook).
- Reporting/dashboard implementation (tracked separately in KPI dashboard spec).

Requirements (HubSpot data model)
A) Entities we will write/modify
1) Company object (primary target)
- We will attach each signal as a Company timeline event + update a small set of roll-up properties for filtering/queues.
- We will NOT create/update Contact records as part of the signal pipeline (avoid PII expansion; outreach uses existing contacts or sales-sourced contacts).

2) Optional: Custom object for PLG Signals (recommended for v1.1)
- If we hit limitations with timeline-only (filtering/reporting), we should create a custom object “PLG Signal” associated to Company.
- v1 can ship with timeline events + company rollups; custom object can be added once we confirm reporting needs.

B) Required Company properties (create if missing)
(Names below are proposed internal names; David K. to map to HubSpot API names and confirm types.)
1) plg_signal_last_seen_at (datetime)
- Updated on each qualifying signal event (post-dedupe).

2) plg_signal_last_type (enumeration)
- Values: spend_growth, sustained_spend, concurrency_burst, repeated_429, error_rate_pain, model_routing_failures, pricing_intent, contact_sales, security_intent, residency_intent, dedicated_docs_intent, private_docs_intent
- Note: keep list tight; types must match scoring service output.

3) plg_signal_score (number)
- 0–100 overall score from scoring service.

4) plg_signal_tier (enumeration)
- Values: p0_high_intent, p1_sales_worthy, p2_nurture (or similar); used for workflow branching.

5) plg_signal_cooldown_until (datetime)
- If set in the future, workflows must not create new tasks/enroll sequences.

6) plg_signal_suppressed (boolean)
- True if account is explicitly suppressed (CS-managed enterprise, legal opt-out, sensitive account flag, etc.).

7) plg_signal_source_env (enumeration)
- hosted_api | dedicated | private | unknown (for expansion vs new logo handling).

8) plg_signal_summary (multi-line text)
- Human-readable one-liner from pipeline for SDR/AEs (e.g., “7d spend +62% and 14d 429 rate 3.2%; suggested: Dedicated eval”). Keep short.

9) plg_signal_last_event_id (single-line text)
- Idempotency/debug hook: last emitted idempotency key to help support investigate duplicates.

C) Timeline events (Company)
- Event name convention: “PLG Signal: <Type>”
- Event body must include (no user-level identifiers):
  - signal_type
  - score
  - window (7d/14d/30d)
  - key metrics (e.g., spend_usd_30d, tokens_30d, p95_latency_ms_7d, rate_limit_hits_7d, concurrency_p95_7d)
  - recommended_next_step (Dedicated / Private / troubleshooting / nurture)
  - links: console/account page (internal), runbook, and (if exists) open support ticket ID
- Keep payload small enough to avoid HubSpot size limits; avoid raw time series.

Workflow expectations (automation)
A) Triggering
- Primary workflow trigger: Company property plg_signal_last_seen_at is known AND plg_signal_score >= threshold AND plg_signal_suppressed != true AND now() > plg_signal_cooldown_until.
- Dedupe is handled upstream (ENG-2842), but HubSpot workflows must also be safe if the same company is updated multiple times in a short period.

B) Actions on qualifying signal
1) Create task
- Task title format: “Follow up: PLG signal – <type> (score <score>)”
- Task notes: include plg_signal_summary + last 2–3 key metrics + recommended next step + link to company record + any relevant docs.
- Due date: next business day (local to owner where feasible).

2) Enroll into sequence (SDR) OR create AE task (AE-only)
- For SDR-owned segments: enroll company’s primary contact (if exists) into the appropriate SDR sequence (rate-limit pain, spend growth, security intent, etc.).
- If no contact exists: create SDR task “Find contact + enroll in sequence” (do not auto-create contact).
- For AE-owned segments (or expansion accounts with active CSM): create AE task only; do not enroll sequences automatically unless sales leadership approves.

3) Optional Slack notification
- Only for p0_high_intent tier and only if not suppressed; post to #sales with link to HubSpot record and a short summary. (Slack is handled by ENG-2844; this ticket defines the gating rules.)

Ownership logic (routing)
Goal: deterministic routing that matches our sales coverage model and avoids stepping on active opportunities or CSM-owned relationships.

A) Primary owner assignment
- If Company has an active owner in HubSpot (AE assigned) AND lifecycle stage indicates active sales motion (see suppression below): do not reassign.
- Else set Company owner using the following rules (maintained as a mapping table; pilot allowlist overrides):
  1) Segment-based: Enterprise/Strategic → AE owner; SMB/MM → SDR owner + AE as secondary (if that is our standard).
  2) Geo-based: NA → Stephanie Nguyen org; EMEA → Lukas Meyer org.
  3) Residency intent: EU-only / UK-only intent should route to EMEA coverage even if signup geo is NA (flag for review; do not auto-reassign without guardrails).

B) Secondary stakeholders
- If signal_type in {security_intent, residency_intent, private_docs_intent}: add a task note to loop in Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein) upon response/meeting booking; do not auto-assign SE in HubSpot.
- If expansion candidate and CSM-managed: notify #customer-success (optional) and create CSM-facing task instead of SDR sequence.

Suppression rules
Workflows must not create tasks/sequences if any of the following are true:
1) Explicit opt-out
- Company-level “do not contact” / subscription status indicates opt-out.

2) Existing active opportunity
- Company has an open Opportunity/Deal stage in {Discovery, Evaluation, Procurement, Negotiation} (final stage list to be confirmed by Sales Ops).

3) CSM-managed enterprise accounts
- Company flagged as Enterprise customer with active CSM ownership (Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim team) OR marked “CS Managed = true”.

4) Sensitive account handling
- Company flagged “Sensitive / Restricted visibility” OR “Security review only”. In this case:
  - Still record the timeline event.
  - Do not auto-enroll sequences.
  - Only create an internal task for the assigned AE (or Biz Systems queue) if permitted.

5) Cool-down period
- plg_signal_cooldown_until in the future (set by scoring service per signal type).

SLAs / SLOs (operational expectations)
- HubSpot write latency (event → visible in HubSpot): p95 < 10 minutes.
- Task creation latency after event is written: < 15 minutes.
- Sales responsiveness target (process, not system): first touch within 1 business day for p1; within 4 business hours for p0 (pilot only).

Auditability / troubleshooting hooks
- Every task created by workflow must include a stable reference to the signal event id (plg_signal_last_event_id) so Support/Sales Ops can correlate duplicates.
- Engineering will maintain write-audit logs; HubSpot side should not require manual intervention to dedupe day-to-day.

Open questions (need Sales Ops + Security signoff)
1) What is the authoritative “active opportunity” definition in HubSpot (deal pipeline + stages) for suppression?
2) Do we want to enroll sequences at the Company level (via primary contact) or require SDR to pick a contact first in all cases?
3) Residency intent routing: allow auto-route to EMEA or only create a review task?
4) Sensitive accounts: should timeline events be visible to all sales users, or restricted via teams/permissions?

Acceptance criteria
- Biz Systems confirms the final property list (names + types) and creates them in HubSpot (or documents existing equivalents).
- Ownership mapping rules are documented in a single source (table) and validated by Sales leadership (Stephanie, Lukas) for pilot.
- A workflow exists that: (a) gates on suppression + cooldown, (b) creates a task with required template, (c) optionally enrolls in the correct sequence when contact exists, and (d) does not create duplicates under repeated updates.
- Security review (Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin) signs off on which fields are allowed in timeline/task notes (no user-level identifiers; minimal account metadata).

References
- Confluence PRD: PLG→Sales signal routing PRD (signals, goals, metrics)
- Confluence design spec: Signal scoring + routing technical design (idempotency keys, cooldown logic)
- Sales enablement: PLG signal follow-up playbook (cadence + sequences)
- Internal support: INT-441 (property/workflow setup request)
